title: Direct vs Regular Mutual Funds: Understanding SEBI’s New Default Plan Rule
description: Regular mutual funds involve a distributor who earns a commission, leading to a higher expense ratio for investors. Direct mutual funds have no distributor co.

faq.a: An EOP is a technology-driven platform approved by SEBI that facilitates transactions in direct mutual fund plans without offering any investment advice or recommendations. Its primary role is to execute buy, sell, and switch orders for direct plans.

faq.q: Is it always better to invest in direct plans?
faq.a: Financially, direct plans are almost always better due to lower expense ratios and higher potential returns. However, they require investors to do their own research and make investment decisions without a distributor's advice.

faq.q: Can I switch my existing regular mutual fund investments to direct plans?
faq.a: Yes, you can. This typically involves selling your units from the regular plan and then purchasing units in the direct plan of the same scheme. Be mindful of potential exit loads and capital gains tax implications when making such a switch.

faq.q: What are the tax implications of switching from a regular to a direct plan?
faq.a: Switching from a regular to a direct plan is treated as a redemption and a fresh purchase. This means any capital gains realised on the sale of your regular plan units will be subject to capital gains tax as per current income tax laws.

faq.q: Do I need a financial advisor if I invest in direct plans?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but it depends on your comfort level with self-directed investing. If you prefer professional guidance for portfolio construction, goal planning, and periodic reviews, you can still engage a SEBI-registered investment advisor (RIA) who charges a fee for advice, rather than earning commissions from your investments.
